newsitem.title: USA: Repair crews work to plug Texas gas leak.
newsitem.headline: Repair crews work to plug Texas gas leak.

text.p: Repair crews worked on Tuesday to plug a gas leak that forced the evacuation of nearly 4,000 inmates from a state prison near Dayton, Texas.
Chevron Corp. spokesman Jerry Barlow said the company expected to have the leak of highly flammable liquified petroleum gas under control by midday on Wednesday.

The prisoners, who were sent to jails and other facilities in nearby towns, would likely not return to the Dayton prison until Thursday or Friday, or until the danger of explosion had passed, said Texas Department of Criminal Justice spokesman Larry Todd.
They were moved on Monday after a billowing cloud of gas began gushing from a pipeline about half a mile from the prison complex, which houses about 3,800 inmates, 2,500 of them women.
Six people were taken to hospitals with breathing problems, while 26 pregnant inmates were placed in a medical facility for observation, officials said.

The leak began during work on the pipeline, and Chevron's original plan was to let all the gas run out of the 10-mile-long line. But Barlow said workers on Tuesday were to close off the pipe a few hundred yards from the leak with the expectation that the gas would run out in a matter of hours.
"It's a matter of emptying a few hundred yards of pipe instead of 10 miles," he said.
Workers would then repair the leak and once the area was considered safe, the inmates could then return to the prison, he said.
